question: Should OpenClaw expose current-session-only self-compaction as a model-callable `session_status(action: "compact")` mutation?
rationale: Source and proof show the narrow implementation is plausible, but deciding whether a model may abort, compact, and resume its own active session is a product/security boundary choice automation should not make.

options.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
options.body: Allow this current-session-only action after branch refresh, keeping the fail-closed checks and mutation tracking as the accepted boundary.

options.title: Require An Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require an operator/tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer To Continuation Design
options.body: Pause or close this narrow PR if maintainers want broader continuation APIs to own voluntary compaction instead.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
recommendation.body: Allow this current-session-only action after branch refresh, keeping the fail-closed checks and mutation tracking as the accepted boundary.
